Normal human male somatic cells contain 44 autosomes and one X and one Y chromosome, making them diploid. They retain the full genetic information from the zygote (A), have 44 autosomes (C), and are diploid (D).  
However, males have only one X chromosome, which remains active — X chromosome inactivation occurs only in females to balance X-linked gene expression. Therefore, an inactivated X chromosome (B) is not present in male somatic cells.  

Final answer: (B)
